_readme: Provenance for every recorded sound in this folder.
There was no manifest before this file. The twenty-nine mp3s already here
arrived with no recorded source at all: a whole-tree ripgrep for 'pixabay'
returned zero hits in any .ts/.tsx/.md/.json/.mjs/.py. Their `source` is
therefore null rather than guessed, and anyone who knows where they came
from should fill it in rather than leaving it to be re-derived.
`planned` below is the sourcing brief for the thirty-eight trap types that
have no recording and fall back to synthesis. Nothing in it has been
downloaded. Each row names the file to write, the mechanic the sound has to
match, and a Pixabay page to pick from. Move a row into `files` when its
mp3 lands, with the exact sound page URL and its author.

matchedTo.note: Measured across all 16 existing trap mp3s. 13 of 16 sit in this band.

correctionToPriorReport: A previous session reported that SAMPLE_PEAK's docstring claimed -1.5 dBFS
while ffmpeg measured -11.7, and that finding was passed on as a reason to
distrust the docstring. It is inverted, and following it would have shipped
every new trap sound about ten decibels under the existing set.
Measured: SAMPLE_PEAK = 0.8414 is exactly -1.500 dBFS. footstep.mp3 is
exactly -11.7 dBFS. The docstring ITSELF names both of its outliers by file
and by number - footstep at -11.7 and ceiling_fan at -11.4 - and says the
rest are within a decibel of -1.5, which the table above bears out.
The -11.7 figure came from the docstring, not from a contradiction of it.
Level is also partly self-correcting at runtime: peakOf() measures each
decoded file and startSustain divides by it, so a gain argument means the
same output peak whatever the file's own level. Matching -1.5 still matters
for headroom and for the one-shot path.

blockerBeforeAnyOfThisPlays: Dropping a correctly-named mp3 into this folder does NOT upgrade its trap.
and RECORDED is CUE_KEYS + RECORDED_TRAPS + 'ambient', where RECORDED_TRAPS
is a hardcoded list of 15 trap ids. The URL is built after that gate, so for
any of the 38 below the file is never fetched, never decoded and never
played - the trap synthesises forever and the file is dead weight.
Each id below has to be added to RECORDED_TRAPS in lib/audio/AudioManager.ts.
Rows marked "bed": true additionally need a SUSTAINED_TRAPS entry, or they go
down the one-shot path which reserves a voice for the buffer's whole length.
The comment above SUSTAINED_TRAPS records what that already cost once: the
floor fan re-fires every 450 ms, so a 6-second buffer stacked 13 copies,
spent all 16 voices, and silenced the player's own jumps and landings.

downloadAttempt.result: BLOCKED - the free Download button delivered no file on any of four sounds
spread: Chosen to vary the two things that could have made one sound atypical: upload
age and uploader. Ids run 6831 to 310479, so from among the oldest audio on the
site to a recent upload, across four different contributors. All four behaved
identically, so this is not one bad sound.
downloadAttempt.whyThatSound: Cartoon Splat by Universfield, 0:01 - the intended paint_bucket match.
howItWasTried: Isolated Chromium, clean profile, no stored session. Driving the user's own
browser was avoided on purpose: it could have ridden a Pixabay account they
are already signed into, which is logging in by proxy.
Page loaded anonymously, HTTP 200, no bot challenge, header showed Log in / Join.
Cookie consent dismissed with Reject All, the conservative choice, needing no account.
The site's own 'Free download' button was clicked. Nothing else was touched:
no credential typed, no share or social control, no attempt to get around a gate.
whatHappened: The button changes to 'Downloading...' with a spinner and stays there (three of
four; the cuckoo clock fell back to 'Free download').
After ~55s each: no download event on the page, no popup carrying one, and - the
decisive measurement - NO .mp3 request was issued at all. A request listener on
the whole browser context caught zero across all four. The only media fetched
were 200x200 thumbnails. The client-side flow starts and never asks the server
for a file, so there is not even a status code to report.
twoExplanationsThatFitEqually: An ACCOUNT GATE: anonymous visitors get the button but not the file.
AUTOMATION DETECTION: a Playwright-driven Chromium is detectable, and the site
may simply no-op the download for one rather than show an error.
Nothing measured here separates the two, and saying which it is would be a guess
dressed as a finding. They point at the same next step either way, so it was not
worth more of the site's patience to find out: a person in an ordinary browser
fetches these. If it is automation detection - and the silent no-op rather than
an error message mildly favours that - then a human will succeed immediately.
conclusion: Not investigated further, and it MUST NOT be worked around: reconstructing a
cdn.pixabay.com URL to skip the button would circumvent whatever gate is there,
What is NOT claimed: that Pixabay requires an account for audio. Four sounds in
one automated environment is what was tested and all it supports.
The `planned` rows below stand unchanged and are ready for whoever can fetch:
filename, mechanic, brief, URL, bed-or-one-shot and target seconds for all 38.

sourcingRules.download: Free Download button only. Never log in, never enter credentials, never use share or social buttons.
sourcingRules.ifLoginDemanded: Skip that sound, leave the row in `planned`, and set skipped:'requires account'.

urlVerification.verified: URL returned by a web search of pixabay.com, so the page is known to exist and to have results.
urlVerification.unverified-query: URL built from Pixabay's confirmed /sound-effects/search/<terms>/ pattern. The page will resolve; whether it has good hits for this brief is unchecked. Pixabay returns HTTP 403 to non-browser fetches, so these could not be confirmed without opening a browser.

files.note: predates this manifest; peaks -11.7 dBFS, 10 dB under the set
on disk but deliberately NOT in RECORDED_TRAPS: the trap never calls contact()

planned.mechanic: Picks a spot, then commits to it. splash 1.15 over a 3u track.
planned.brief: Wet paint hitting floor, not a metal bucket. The commit is the whole joke, so one fat splat with no ring-out.

planned.mechanic: Winds up loudly, then throws the room. burst 2.2.
planned.brief: Rising drum whine into a thump. The wind-up IS the warning, so the pitch rise must be audible before the hit.

planned.mechanic: Takes your momentum and keeps it. grip 9 over a 0.72u radius, braking every frame you stand in it.
planned.brief: Continuous peeling squelch, not a single splat. Its cost is dwell, so the sound has to last as long as the runner is stuck.

planned.mechanic: Only catches runners in a hurry. Fires above tripSpeed 4.2 across a 1.7u span.
planned.brief: Taut cable snap and whip. Nothing before the trip: silence is what makes it only catch the hasty.

planned.mechanic: Shuts the lane on a schedule. travel 1.35.
planned.brief: Wooden drawer running out then banging home. Two-part - the slide is the tell, the bang is the hit.

planned.mechanic: Waits until both feet are on it, then yanks 1.6.
planned.brief: Heavy fabric ripped sideways across floor. Fast attack, no impact - the runner supplies the landing.

planned.mechanic: Takes you somewhere. carry 3.4 for as long as you stand on 2.4x1.5u of belt.
planned.brief: Rubber belt over rollers, steady, no melody. Runs while the runner is carried, so it must loop seamlessly.

planned.mechanic: Dumps you off whichever side you loaded. tip 4.2 on a 0.9u plate.
planned.brief: Wooden board pivoting and knocking down on its stop. A see-saw clunk, weighted, not a snap.

planned.mechanic: Only sees you if you are moving. reach 3.2, arc 0.55, ignores below stillSpeed 1.4.
planned.brief: Single electronic detection chirp. Short and dry - the information is 'you were seen', and it must cut through a busy mix.

planned.mechanic: Harmless until something else shoves it. 1.8u span, then cascades.
planned.brief: Accelerating clatter of tiles going over. The cascade is the mechanic, so it needs the run, not one tick.

planned.mechanic: Strung at exactly jump height. 2u span, 0.75 clearance.
planned.brief: Cloth flags snagging and string twanging. Light and papery - it catches you, it does not hit you.

planned.mechanic: Three lanes. One of them is lying. blast 0.7, spread 0.95.
planned.brief: Sharp pressurised burst with a hard start. Must be identical every time or the bluff lane becomes readable by ear.

planned.mechanic: MAKES ITS NOISE AT THE SAFE END. 2.6u run, blast 0.9.
planned.brief: Knocking pipe then water letting go. Deliberate misdirection - check with the trap's author that the emitter sits at the safe end, because a sound at the hazard end inverts the trap.

planned.mechanic: You keep these for the rest of the run. reach 0.55, drag 1.6, taxes every step afterwards.
planned.brief: Metal cuff clamping shut with a chain settle. Must sound permanent - a latch, not a bump - because the cost outlives the window.

planned.mechanic: Puts you back where it thinks you belong. 0.8u mouth, setback 2.6.
planned.brief: Body sliding down sheet metal into a drop. Descending, with travel - the runner is being moved, not struck.

planned.mechanic: Copies your sidestep. Every time. travel 1.4 on a 2.2u track.
planned.brief: Trolley castors juddering sideways then hitting the stop. The mirrored move wants a squeak of tracking under the impact.

planned.mechanic: Walks where you walked, a moment late. lag 1600 ms, chase 3.6.
planned.brief: Dry soft rolling scuff. A chaser is present for as long as it chases, so this loops rather than firing per contact.

planned.mechanic: Bigger the longer you dither. Grows 0.055/s from 0.7u to 2u.
planned.brief: Water spreading over a hard floor. Growth is the mechanic, so it wants a loop that reads as ongoing rather than a single splash.

planned.mechanic: Only lifts you once you have left the ground. reach 0.9, lift 4.2, ceiling 2.6.
planned.brief: Column of rushing air, no impact. Airy and continuous - the vent runs whether or not it has caught anyone.

planned.mechanic: Gives your speed back, pointing the other way. bounce 1.15 over 1.8u.
planned.brief: Sprung mattress boing with a fabric thud under it. Comic, pitched, and it must read as a return rather than a stop.

planned.mechanic: One nudge, and the floor is ruined for good. spread 2.4, permanent.
planned.brief: Ceramic smashing and scattering wide. The long scatter tail is the point - it says the floor stays ruined.

planned.mechanic: Crawl or sprint. Anything between hurts. Safe below 2.2 or above 6.
planned.brief: Light plastic flap swinging on its hinge. Cheap and rattly, so the punishment reads as absurd rather than heavy.

planned.mechanic: Takes your picture. Takes your view. reach 3.2, blind 6.
planned.brief: Capacitor whine rising into a shutter and flash pop. The whine is the tell and must precede the blind, so do not trim the head.

planned.mechanic: Ignores your walk. Reads your landing. impact 5 on a 0.95u pad.
planned.brief: Spring platform bottoming out with a dial click. Only fires on a landing, so it wants weight on the front of the sound.

planned.mechanic: Charges you here, collects somewhere else. radius 0.9, blast 1.2, delayed.
planned.brief: Burning fuse hiss and sputter, ENDING IN NOTHING. The bang belongs to the hazard event elsewhere; a bang in this file gives the delay away.

planned.mechanic: Only falls on someone already falling. radius 1.5.
planned.brief: Cascade of junk landing in a heap. Layered and uneven - it is a pile arriving, not one object.

planned.mechanic: Perfectly safe until you step off it. pedal 0.8, swipe 1.4 on release.
planned.brief: Pedal bin lid flying up and clanging back. The trigger is the STEP OFF, so the sound starts at the release.

planned.mechanic: Lets you through, then changes its mind. 1.9u span.
planned.brief: Sprung door swinging past and slamming back. The return is the hit, so the slam sits at the end, not the start.

planned.mechanic: Fires at where you are going to be. range 3.6, spread 0.85.
planned.brief: Pneumatic thunk and ball leaving the barrel. Dry and repeatable - it fires often, so no long tail.

planned.mechanic: Chimes twice. BITES ON THE THIRD. reach 1.5.
planned.brief: Two cuckoo calls then the mechanism. The count is the whole tell, so the file must carry all three beats and stay identical every cycle.

planned.mechanic: Hates a runner who keeps changing pace. jolt 18 within 1.5u.
planned.brief: Water sloshing hard inside glass then the bowl going over. jolt 18 is the heaviest impulse of the 38, so this is the loudest of the set.

planned.mechanic: Kicks you into the spot it lands on. reach 2.2, crush 1.3, offset 1.5.
planned.brief: Rack tipping and shoes tumbling out. Soft leather clatter, not crockery - it displaces you rather than shattering.

planned.mechanic: Harmless until something moves it. blast 1.1 once disturbed.
planned.brief: Sudden sizzle flaring up. Dormant then hot, so the attack has to be instant with no ramp.

planned.mechanic: The only safe spot is the middle. eye 0.55 safe, flare 1.7 around it.
planned.brief: Gas ring lit and burning steadily. Continuous - the ring is always on, and the safe eye is spatial not temporal.

planned.mechanic: Ignores runners. CATCHES DODGERS. length 2.1, sidestep 2.6.
planned.brief: Thin metal frame collapsing with laundry. Rattly and light - it only ever catches someone already moving sideways.

planned.mechanic: One magazine, then it is furniture. range 4.5, spread 1.3, finite.
planned.brief: Ice cubes clattering out of a chute and stopping. Running dry must be audible - the tail is how a player learns it is spent.

planned.mechanic: Comes to the boil on its own schedule. scald 1.9.
planned.brief: Water building to a rolling boil and a whistle. A LONG BUILD, which is why it must be a bed - as a one-shot it holds a voice for its whole length and starves the mix.

planned.mechanic: Grows on whatever is standing near it. base 0.75, feed 4.5.
planned.brief: Loose debris shifting and accumulating. Ongoing accretion, so it loops for as long as the drift is being fed.
